speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a pruritic rash, fever, rhinorrhea, and headache; to narrow this down, have you noticed any specific pattern to your rash or any joint pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease).

The description of a rash starting on the trunk/extremities followed by a "slapped cheek" facial rash sparing the perioral area, combined with recent viral prodrome, is classic for Parvovirus B19. The pruritus is also commonly reported. Do you have any concerns regarding the patient's anemia or family history of sickle cell disease?
